project: Runtime Taxonomy Worker And Workstation Split
description: Introduce clear public worker and workstation taxonomy that separates one-shot inference behavior from agentic behavior, preserves existing factory compatibility through aliases and projection, represents OmniVoice as default inference behavior, and reserves AGENT_WORKER plus AGENT_RUN for future agent-loop execution.

context.customerAsk: Separate default inference behavior from agentic behavior in factory configuration. Introduce clear public names for inference, agent, script, and poller behavior; preserve existing factory compatibility; make OmniVoice a default inference worker rather than an agent worker; and leave a distinct AGENT_WORKER and AGENT_RUN path for future llama.cpp agent work.
context.problem: The current MODEL_WORKER and MODEL_INVOKE names conflate harnessless inference calls with future agent loops, make OmniVoice look like an agent worker, and leave validation, dashboard labels, docs, and generated contracts without a clear customer-facing distinction between inference, agent, script, and poller behavior.
context.solution: Add INFERENCE_WORKER, AGENT_WORKER, SCRIPT_WORKER, and POLLER_WORKER plus INFERENCE_RUN, AGENT_RUN, SCRIPT_RUN, and POLLER_RUN to the public factory contract. Map legacy MODEL_WORKER to inference-worker behavior, MODEL_INVOKE to inference-run behavior, and existing hosted/poller behavior to poller compatibility while keeping runtime behavior paths unified and updating validation, UI projections, docs, examples, generated clients, and tests.

acceptanceCriteria: Public factory config, API payloads, generated Go types, and generated TypeScript types accept the new worker and workstation taxonomy while continuing to accept legacy names.
Legacy factories using MODEL_WORKER, MODEL_INVOKE, and existing hosted or poller vocabulary load, validate, execute, and save without requiring customer edits.
New factory creation, projection, UI labels, reference docs, and examples prefer INFERENCE_WORKER, INFERENCE_RUN, AGENT_WORKER, AGENT_RUN, SCRIPT_WORKER, SCRIPT_RUN, POLLER_WORKER, and POLLER_RUN.
Validation rejects incompatible worker/workstation pairings and explains failures with inference, agent, script, or poller terminology.
Dashboard graph projections and current-factory save round trips preserve workstation identity, worker identity, and layout references when new or legacy names are used.
OmniVoice defaults are represented as inference worker/run behavior, and agent vocabulary remains reserved for future agent-loop execution.
Quality gate: generated contracts are current, typecheck passes, lint passes, focused backend/API/UI/docs tests pass, and changed browser-visible UI is verified in browser.

userStories.title: Accept the new worker taxonomy while preserving legacy worker aliases
userStories.description: As a factory author, I want worker type names that describe whether a worker performs inference, agent, script, or poller behavior so that factory config is clear without breaking existing factories.
acceptanceCriteria: Public factory config accepts INFERENCE_WORKER, AGENT_WORKER, SCRIPT_WORKER, and POLLER_WORKER anywhere worker type values are accepted.
Existing factories that use MODEL_WORKER, SCRIPT_WORKER, or HOSTED_WORKER continue to load and validate successfully.
MODEL_WORKER projects to inference-worker behavior unless an explicit future agent migration rule identifies otherwise.
HOSTED_WORKER compatibility preserves existing poller behavior while allowing new factories to use POLLER_WORKER.
API enum contract tests and config mapping tests cover new worker names and legacy worker aliases with observable load/projection outcomes.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Accept the new workstation taxonomy while preserving legacy run aliases
userStories.description: As a factory author, I want workstation behavior names that distinguish one-shot inference, agent runs, scripts, and pollers so that factory workflow behavior is clear and legacy workstations still execute.
acceptanceCriteria: Public factory config accepts INFERENCE_RUN, AGENT_RUN, SCRIPT_RUN, and POLLER_RUN anywhere workstation type values are accepted.
Existing factories using MODEL_INVOKE continue to load, validate, and execute as inference-run behavior.
Existing poller workstations continue to load, validate, and execute as poller-run compatibility behavior.

Saved current-factory documents round-trip new workstation type names without being downgraded to legacy names unless the user opened a legacy factory and the compatibility policy requires legacy preservation.
API enum contract tests and config mapping tests cover new workstation names and legacy workstation aliases with observable load/projection outcomes.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Enforce worker and workstation compatibility with behavior-specific validation
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want validation to reject incompatible worker/workstation pairings with behavior-specific messages so authors can fix inference, agent, script, or poller mistakes directly.
acceptanceCriteria: Validation accepts compatible pairings: INFERENCE_RUN with INFERENCE_WORKER, AGENT_RUN with AGENT_WORKER, SCRIPT_RUN with SCRIPT_WORKER, and POLLER_RUN with POLLER_WORKER, including their supported legacy aliases.
Validation rejects incompatible pairings such as AGENT_RUN with INFERENCE_WORKER, INFERENCE_RUN with AGENT_WORKER, and POLLER_RUN with non-poller workers.
Validation messages for new config use the new inference, agent, script, and poller terms and identify the incompatible worker and workstation values.
Legacy config still reports actionable validation findings without forcing immediate migration to new names.
Tests cover invalid pairings, legacy aliases, and saved round trips using behavior assertions instead of source-file inventories.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

Dashboard graph projections preserve the same identity and layout references after loading legacy MODEL_WORKER, MODEL_INVOKE, and hosted/poller-compatible factories.
New factory creation and editor controls prefer new taxonomy labels and values for inference, agent, script, and poller behavior.
Loading, empty, validation-error, save-error, and successful-save states remain explicit when taxonomy-related values are edited.
Keyboard-operable selection and save flows remain available for changed taxonomy controls, and labels make the selected behavior class clear to assistive technology.
Focused UI tests cover projection/save behavior for new and legacy values, and direct browser verification confirms visible labels and save states.

userStories.title: Update docs and examples to teach inference, agent, script, and poller behavior
userStories.description: As a factory author, I want docs and examples to use the new taxonomy so I learn the intended vocabulary without being pushed toward legacy model-worker names.
acceptanceCriteria: Public reference docs explain INFERENCE_WORKER/INFERENCE_RUN, AGENT_WORKER/AGENT_RUN, SCRIPT_WORKER/SCRIPT_RUN, and POLLER_WORKER/POLLER_RUN in customer-facing terms.
Docs describe legacy MODEL_WORKER, MODEL_INVOKE, and hosted/poller compatibility as aliases during the migration window rather than removed behavior.
OmniVoice or default inference examples use inference worker/run terminology and do not describe harnessless inference as agent behavior.
Future agent examples or placeholders use AGENT_WORKER and AGENT_RUN only for agent-loop behavior and do not imply llama.cpp supervision is part of this project.
Packaged reference-doc smoke checks pass for changed docs.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Prove runtime execution uses inference behavior for OmniVoice and reserves agent behavior for agent runs
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want runtime tests to prove new taxonomy values execute through the intended behavior paths so compatibility aliases do not mask inference and agent behavior regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: A configured INFERENCE_WORKER with an INFERENCE_RUN workstation executes one bounded inference operation and emits the same observable work result shape as the legacy MODEL_WORKER plus MODEL_INVOKE compatibility path.
OmniVoice default configuration or fixture behavior is represented as inference worker/run behavior and does not require agent-loop fields to execute.
A configured AGENT_RUN does not execute against an inference worker and fails validation before dispatch with an actionable compatibility finding.
Legacy MODEL_WORKER plus MODEL_INVOKE execution remains covered and produces inference-run behavior during the migration window.
Runtime tests verify dispatch outcome, emitted events, and routed output instead of asserting helper or package topology.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
